findings.reason: The protected app-local and Accepted native sources are the canonical one-expression solution: positivity excludes zero and negatives, while n & (n - 1) recognizes exactly one set bit. The code is maximally concise, conventional, and fixed-width O(1)-time/O(1)-space, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local function and native class method contain the identical Boolean expression and differ only by the required LeetCode class wrapper. Submission evidence is verified and the native source remains unchanged.

The former 1/8/30-bit benchmark could not reject repeated division: that correct O(log n) control still passed at +0.06 relative exponent. Because the source contract fixes n to a signed 32-bit domain, a bounded-domain certificate now proves that the protected source always executes one comparison, one subtraction, and one bitwise AND.

The Approach accurately proves both directions of the least-significant-set-bit identity, explicitly ties O(1) to fixed-width integers, and now labels non-positive and one-value boundaries separately.
